newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik peace talks suspended a second time.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks suspended a second time.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Thursday peace talks between Tajikistan's government and the republic's armed Islamic opposition had been suspended for the second time in under two weeks.
"There will be a two week break (in the talks)," Velayati told reporters on his arrival in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.
Iran has been hosting the latest round of talks in Tehran, aimed at dragging the former Soviet republic of 5.7 million out of a devastating four-year civil war which has killed tens of thousands.
Velayati, on a lightning visit to the republic, gave no reason for the pause in the talks, which were only restarted on Wednesday.
But the United Nations, which sponsors the talks, said in a statement that the halt had been agreed to give both sides more time for consultations with their respective leaderships.
The U.N. said talks would resume in Tehran on May 16.
The negotiations stopped almost as soon as they began on April 9 after opposition negotiator Akbar Turajonzoda alleged 11 opposition members had been arrested in Moscow on charges of "terrorism".

The government and Islamic opposition guerrillas agreed a ceasefire in December last year. Unlike earlier accords, which were regularly flouted, the ceasefire has largely held. The two sides even agreed a preliminary power-sharing agreement in February.

But diplomats in the Tajik capital warned earlier this month that the political issues on the current round's agenda, especially the legalisation of opposition parties in the republic, could stall the talks.
